differential.name: Diabetic kidney disease (diabetic nephropathy)
differential.rationale: Long‑standing type 2 diabetes with proteinuria/microalbuminuria and progressive CKD stages 1‑4 is classic for diabetic nephropathy.

differential.name: Hypertensive nephrosclerosis
differential.rationale: Co‑existing essential hypertension and CKD progression in a Black patient make hypertensive renal damage a strong contributor.

differential.name: Chronic glomerulonephritis (e.g., IgA nephropathy)
differential.rationale: Persistent proteinuria with gradual loss of renal function can be due to an underlying glomerular disease not yet specified.

differential.name: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
differential.rationale: Family history not given, but cystic disease can present with CKD stages 1‑4 and may coexist with diabetes/hypertension.

differential.name: Obstructive uropathy (e.g., nephrolithiasis or ureteral stricture)
differential.rationale: Can cause progressive renal insufficiency and proteinuria, though less likely without imaging or pain localization.
